title: Basilicata
quiz.0.question: In what geological setting is Aglianico del Vulture grown?
quiz.0.options.1: The slopes of an extinct volcano
quiz.0.explanation: Aglianico del Vulture comes from the slopes of the extinct volcano Monte Vulture, whose volcanic soils give the wines a distinctive minerality.
quiz.1.question: When can Aglianico del Vulture Superiore Riserva first be released?
quiz.1.explanation: Superiore Riserva must be aged at least 2 years in wood and 1 year in bottle, and cannot be released before the fifth year after harvest; Superiore requires 1 year in wood + 1 year in bottle and release from 1 November of the third year.

quiz.2.options.1: The same grape, but different biotypes (Aglianico del Vulture and Aglianico di Taurasi)
quiz.2.explanation: Both are Aglianico, from two different biotypes: Aglianico del Vulture and Aglianico di Taurasi. Aglianico del Vulture requires 100% Aglianico, whereas Taurasi requires a minimum of 85%.
quiz.3.question: What is the signature spice of Basilicata’s cuisine?
quiz.3.explanation: Basilicata’s cuisine is known for chilli (peperoncino), and peperoni cruschi (crispy dried peppers) are a local speciality; IWS also highlights Canestrato di Moliterno cheese, Lucanica sausage and Matera bread.
slides.0.title: 🌋 Basilicata
slides.0.subtitle: The Only Home of Aglianico del Vulture
slides.1.title: 🏔️ Italy’s Proud Hidden Region
slides.1.content:
Basilicata, historically known as Lucania, has one of Italy’s smallest areas under vine and smallest wine volumes, yet it is home to Aglianico del Vulture — one of southern Italy’s most important Aglianico appellations. It borders Campania and Puglia to the north and Calabria to the south.

🎯 Two coasts: a small strip on the Ionian Sea (between Salento and Calabria) and a tiny stretch on the Tyrrhenian Sea; two provinces, Potenza and Matera.

slides.2.title: 🗺️ Basilicata DOCG & DOC Interactive Map
slides.3.title: 🌋 The Two Appellations of Aglianico del Vulture
slides.3.content:
Aglianico del Vulture became a DOC in 1971; in 2010 only the Superiore category was elevated to DOCG. Both appellations require 100% Aglianico. Volcanic soils, abundant sunlight and a wide diurnal range are the pillars of quality.

🍷 Aglianico del Vulture DOC (1971)

  • Grape: 100% Aglianico
  • Release: not before 1 September of the year after harvest
  • Note: many wines — including some top bottlings — are still released as DOC
  • Also: a sparkling (spumante) version is permitted
  • Price: €15-25

⭐ Aglianico del Vulture Superiore DOCG (2010)

  • Rules: lower maximum yield, higher minimum ABV, longer ageing
  • Ageing: at least 1 year in wood + at least 1 year in bottle
  • Release: not before 1 November of the third year after harvest
  • Price: €25-45

🏆 Superiore Riserva

  • Ageing: at least 2 years in wood + at least 1 year in bottle
  • Release: not before the fifth year after harvest
  • Style: complex, refined, age-worthy
  • Price: €50-100
slides.4.title: 🍷 Label Example: Aglianico del Vulture DOC
slides.4.caption: Paternoster “Synthesi” Aglianico del Vulture DOC 2015 — Paternoster is a historic estate in Barile; Aglianico del Vulture DOC requires 100% Aglianico, and many top wines are still bottled as DOC. The label reads “Denominazione di Origine Controllata”: the DOC level (only the Superiore category is DOCG).
slides.5.title: ⏳ How Aglianico del Vulture Ages
slides.5.content:
🍷 From fiery youth to legendary elder

Young Aglianico del Vulture has firm tannins and can be hard to approach; it needs time to show its true character. Aglianico is thick-skinned and late-ripening; Aglianico del Vulture is high in acidity and tannin, with more pronounced red fruit — complex, refined and age-worthy.

🌑 Youth (1-5 years)

Deep purple-black, with powerful, gripping tannins and high acidity; decant for 1-2 hours. Blackberry, violet and mineral notes dominate — a grand structure, not yet in balance.

Tip: decant for at least 2 hours
🟣 Maturity (6-15 years)

A garnet rim appears and the tannins begin to soften as complexity builds quickly. Leather, tobacco and toasty oak intertwine, the minerality becomes more prominent, and the wine reaches its first drinking peak.

The best window for Superiore
💎 Old age (15-30 years)

Elegant and fine, with silky tannins. Tar, truffle, dried roses and volcanic-ash minerality merge — among southern Italy’s most age-worthy reds, and where the Riserva reaches legendary heights.

The ultimate goal for Riserva collectors
slides.6.title: 🆚 Vulture vs Taurasi: One Grape, Two Souls
slides.6.content:
🤔 Aglianico del Vulture (Basilicata) and Taurasi (Campania) are both made from Aglianico, from two of its three main biotypes: Aglianico del Vulture and Aglianico di Taurasi (the third is Taburno’s Aglianico Amaro). Different biotypes, soils and climates give them different personalities.

🏔️ Taurasi DOCG (Campania)

  • Biotype: Aglianico di Taurasi
  • Soils: calcareous clays and marine limestone mixed with volcanic material
  • Elevation: 300-700 m, moderated by the Calore river
  • Rules: min. 85% Aglianico; min. 3 years (1 in wood)
  • Style: structured, powerful, full-bodied
  • Status: southern Italy’s first DOCG (1993)

🌋 Aglianico del Vulture (Basilicata)

  • Biotype: Aglianico del Vulture (once thought to be a distinct variety)
  • Soils: volcanic in the west, sandy clay in the east
  • Climate: mainly continental, abundant sunlight, wide diurnal range
  • Rules: 100% Aglianico
  • Style: high acidity and tannin, more pronounced red fruit, complex, refined, age-worthy
  • Status: DOC in 1971; Superiore elevated to DOCG in 2010
slides.7.title: 🍷 Other Basilicata DOCs
slides.7.content:
🏛️ Matera DOC (2005)

In eastern Basilicata near the border with Apulia, home of the UNESCO World Heritage city of Matera and its cave dwellings (the Sassi).

  • Red grapes: Primitivo, Sangiovese; plus Moro (a Cabernet Sauvignon-based red category)
  • White grapes: Malvasia, Greco
  • Soils: mainly limestone around Matera
  • Pairing: Matera bread, lamb, aged cheeses

🕳️ Grottino di Roccanova DOC

“Grottino” means “little cave”, after the traditional cave cellars; in south-western Basilicata, with tiny production.

  • Main grapes: Sangiovese, Malvasia Nera, Cabernet Sauvignon
  • White grapes: Malvasia Bianca, Greco
  • Key fact: very small production, mostly sold locally

🏔️ Terre dell'Alta Val d'Agri DOC

In the upper Agri valley, a DOC based on international grapes.

  • Main grapes: Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon, Malvasia
  • Style: a mountain area based on international grapes
  • Key fact: international varieties play only a minor role in Basilicata
slides.8.title: 🥂 Aglianico del Vulture Spumante — a Hidden Gem
slides.8.content:
Aglianico del Vulture DOC permits sparkling wine (spumante) — one of the differences between the DOC and the Superiore DOCG. Production is tiny, making it a unique find for wine lovers.

🍾 Metodo Classico (traditional method)

  • Method: second fermentation in bottle (as in Champagne)
  • Ageing: depends on the producer
  • Colour: pale rose-pink, with fine, persistent bubbles
  • Style: elegant, mineral, high acidity
  • Flavours: red berries, bread and yeast, minerality, volcanic ash
  • Price: €25-45

🥂 Metodo Charmat (tank method)

  • Method: second fermentation in stainless-steel tanks
  • Release: quicker
  • Style: fresh, fruity, easy-drinking
  • Flavours: cherry, strawberry, violet
  • Key fact: better suited to summer, an entry-level Aglianico sparkler
  • Example: entry-level Aglianico spumante (€12-22)
slides.9.title: 🍽️ Basilicata Food and Wine Pairing
slides.9.content:
Basilicata’s cuisine is rustic and fiery, built on chilli (peperoncino), lamb, pork and handmade pasta — the most characterful mountain country cooking in southern Italy.

🐑 Agnello al Forno (roast lamb) × Aglianico del Vulture Superiore

Lamb roasted with rosemary, garlic and chilli is Basilicata’s signature dish. The Superiore’s tannins cut through the fat, and its minerality echoes the wild mountain herbs — a perfect match.

🌶️ Lucanica sausage × young Aglianico / Matera Primitivo

Spicy pork sausage (already recorded in Roman times; “Lucanica” is the ancestor of modern salsiccia) with young Aglianico: fierce spice and fruity tannins in perfect balance.

🍝 Lagane e Ceci (wide pasta with chickpeas) × Matera Greco / Aglianico Rosato

A traditional Basilicata pasta: wide noodles in a chickpea stew, simple and warming. Matera Greco brings out the freshness of the broth; an Aglianico rosato adds depth.

🌶️ Peperoni Cruschi × any Basilicata wine

Peperoni cruschi (crispy dried peppers) are Basilicata’s most iconic speciality: fried until crunchy and not hot, a must on the local table. Any Basilicata wine will do.
slides.10.title: 📜 Basilicata Wine History in Depth
slides.10.content:
Basilicata was historically called “Lucania”, a name still used today. From Greek colonisation, the Lucani and the Romans to the DOC and DOCG of the 20th and 21st centuries, Aglianico del Vulture has always been at its heart.

“Basilicata has one of Italy’s smallest areas under vine, yet Aglianico del Vulture earns it a place among southern Italy’s great wines.”

8th c. BCE

🏺 The Greeks settle

The Greeks established coastal settlements in the 8th century BCE (the Tavole Palatine temple at Metaponto still stands); in the 6th-5th centuries BCE they were repelled by the native Lucani.

3rd c. BCE

🏛️ Annexed by Rome

The area was annexed by the Romans in the 3rd century BCE and is still referred to as Lucania. The Roman poet Horace was born in Venosa, in today’s Vulture area.

1971

📜 Aglianico del Vulture DOC

Aglianico del Vulture became a DOC in 1971, requiring 100% Aglianico.

2010-today

🌟 Superiore elevated to DOCG

In 2010 the Superiore category was elevated to DOCG, with lower yields, higher alcohol and longer ageing; in 2019 Matera was European Capital of Culture.

slides.11.title: 🍇 Basilicata’s Grape Varieties (IWS Course Material)
slides.11.content:
🍇 Over 70% red, with Aglianico in the lead

Aglianico

  • Status: Basilicata’s most widely planted grape
  • Traits: thick-skinned and late-ripening, high in acidity and tannin; great intravarietal variability
  • Soils: prefers volcanic soils
  • Nickname: “the Barolo of the South”

The Aglianico del Vulture biotype

  • Status: one of Aglianico’s three main biotypes (with Aglianico di Taurasi and Aglianico Amaro)
  • History: originally thought to be a genetically distinct variety
  • Style: high acidity and tannin, more pronounced red fruit; complex, refined, age-worthy
  • Note: Basilicata’s Aglianico is the same variety as Campania’s

🔬 Other varieties

⚪ Malvasia Bianca di Basilicata

Rare and Basilicata’s most distinctive white grape, unrelated to other Malvasias. Small amounts were traditionally blended with Aglianico to soften the wine.

The most distinctive white
🍷 Other red grapes

Primitivo, Sangiovese, Montepulciano, Malvasia Nera di Basilicata, Ciliegiolo, Barbera and others.

Primitivo in Matera DOC
🌍 International varieties

Play a minor role, mainly in Matera DOC’s Moro and in Terre dell'Alta Val d'Agri DOC.

Merlot, Cabernet Sauvignon
slides.12.title: 🌋 Location, Topography, Climate and Soils (IWS Course Material)
slides.12.content:
🌋 Nearly half the region is mountains (the Appennino Lucano, i.e. the Southern Apennines). The extinct volcano Monte Vulture rises in the north-west, and there is a small coastal plain (Metapontino) by the Ionian Sea. The climate is mainly continental, with Mediterranean influence only on the small Ionian coastal strip in the east; the diurnal range is big.

🌋

The Aglianico del Vulture area

  • Location: the northernmost part of Basilicata; 15 villages around the ancient extinct volcano Monte Vulture
  • Terroir: volcanic soils, abundant sunlight, wide diurnal range; the twin Monticchio lakes lie in the crater
  • MGAs: 70 Menzioni Geografiche Aggiuntive (additional geographical units)
  • Rainfall: highest in the west, around Vulture and Potenza
⛰️

Two main areas

  • Vulture area (west): higher elevations, volcanic soils, refined and complex wines
  • Eastern area: lower elevations, sandy clay soils, fuller and more generous wines
  • Rivers: the Bradano, Basento, Agri and others flow east into the Ionian Sea

🔑 Basilicata’s soils

slides.13.title: 🏘️ The DOCG’s Core Villages
slides.13.content:
⭐ Barile

One of the core villages of the Vulture area, home to both Elena Fucci and Paternoster. Elena Fucci’s Titolo comes from Barile’s Contrada Solagna del Titolo.

Volcanic soils · Vulture area (west)

Key wines: Elena Fucci Titolo, Paternoster Don Anselmo

🍇 Rionero in Vulture

One of the area’s main towns, home to D'Angelo and Cantine del Notaio.

Volcanic soils · historic estates

Key wines: Cantine del Notaio Il Repertorio, D'Angelo Vigna Caselle

📜 Venosa (birthplace of Horace)

Birthplace of the Roman poet Horace (65-8 BCE), in the east of the area, at lower elevation with mainly sandy clay soils and fuller, more generous wines.

Eastern area · rich history

Producers: Cantina di Venosa (cooperative), Grifalco

🌿 Rapolla, Melfi, Ripacandida, Ginestra

Other villages around Monte Vulture; the whole area has 15 villages and 70 MGAs.

15 villages · 70 MGAs

Key wine: Grifalco Daginestra (Ginestra)

slides.15.title: 🍽️ In-depth Pairing Guide & 🗺️ Wine Route
slides.15.content:
🌶️ The Basilicata table: the fierce beauty of the mountains

Basilicata’s cuisine has chilli, lamb and pork at its soul; paired with Aglianico’s powerful tannins and minerality, it makes southern Italy’s most fiery and moving food-and-wine combinations.

🐑 Agnello al Forno (roast lamb) × Aglianico del Vulture Superiore Riserva

Basilicata’s signature dish, seasoned with rosemary, garlic and chilli and slow-roasted for 3-4 hours. The Riserva’s silky tannins and tarry minerality cut through the lamb fat — the classic southern Italian match. Decant for 2-3 hours.

🍄 Pasta with porcini & black truffle × DOCG Superiore

Wide pasta with porcini and black truffle, an autumn dish of Basilicata’s mountains. The Superiore’s earthy minerality naturally echoes the truffle — the ultimate way to enjoy Aglianico.

🧀 Canestrato di Moliterno (aged cheese) × DOCG Riserva

Basilicata’s mixed-milk (sheep and goat) cheese, aged 6-18 months, salty and firm. The Riserva’s firm tannins cut the fat and its minerality echoes the savouriness — the most traditional local pairing.

🌶️ Cinghiale (wild-boar stew) × young Aglianico del Vulture

Wild boar stewed with chilli, bay leaves and red wine, a festive autumn-winter dish. Young Aglianico’s generous fruit and high tannins balance the boar’s gamey flavour — better here than a Riserva.

🗺️ Basilicata wine route

🌋 Two days around Vulture: Day 1 in Barile: Elena Fucci and Paternoster (book ahead) + a traditional osteria. Day 2 in Rionero: D'Angelo and Cantine del Notaio, then Venosa, Horace’s birthplace.
🏛️ Matera, UNESCO World Heritage: the cave city of the Sassi (European Capital of Culture 2019); arrive early to see sunrise gild the caves, then visit Matera DOC wineries — the perfect blend of culture and wine.
🏖️ The Ionian coast + Metaponto: Basilicata has a short Ionian coastline, and Metaponto has well-preserved Magna Graecia remains (the Tavole Palatine temple) — the best place to understand the region’s Greek roots.
📅 Best time to visit: September-October, at harvest, when the weather is pleasant. A hire car (with GPS) is essential; Bari airport is 1.5 hours away. English is not widely spoken, so a translation app helps.
slides.16.title: 🎓 Key Takeaways

slides.16.points.1: ✓ Nearly half is mountains (Appennino Lucano); two coasts, the Ionian and a tiny stretch of Tyrrhenian; mainly continental, with a big diurnal range
slides.16.points.2: ✓ Soils: volcanic at Vulture, clay and limestone in the hills, limestone around Matera, sandy and alluvial on the south-east coast
slides.16.points.3: ✓ Reds make up 70%+ and Aglianico is the most planted; Malvasia Bianca di Basilicata is the most distinctive white, unrelated to other Malvasias
slides.16.points.4: ✓ Aglianico del Vulture is one of Aglianico’s three main biotypes: high acidity and tannin, more pronounced red fruit, complex, refined, age-worthy
slides.16.points.5: ✓ The area is in the far north of Basilicata: 15 villages around the extinct Monte Vulture, 70 MGAs; volcanic west more refined, sandy-clay east fuller
slides.16.points.6: ✓ Aglianico del Vulture DOC (1971) and Superiore DOCG (2010) both require 100% Aglianico; the DOC can be released from 1 September of the year after harvest
slides.16.points.7: ✓ Superiore: 1 year in wood + 1 in bottle, released from 1 November of year three; Riserva: 2 years in wood + 1 in bottle, released from year five
